description: CORRECTED 2026-08-23 after checking the consuming layer. The observation stands: seven gaps are held pending and the picker re-selects and skips them roughly 600 times a day (432 picks of route-edit-56849210 in 48h, never composed). Two mechanism claims were wrong and are withdrawn: it is not a sweep failure (zero sweep errors in the last 6h; the ConnectionRefused burst was a 17-minute activity-api outage on 08-22 08:33-08:50), and it is not a stale flag (pending_set_at re-stamps to the current minute on every sweep). The real mechanism: verifyGapCondition at gap-to-feature.ts:1149 RE-DERIVES pending from git on every pick via landedCommitVerdict — one non-reverted landing yields pending, two or more yields present — so pending is a function of commit history and cannot be cleared by writing gap metadata. I verified this by writing disposition and pending_set_at and watching the picker log PENDING verification one minute later regardless. Two real exits, both already in the design: (1) give the edit_intent_route class a measurement predicate — evidence_resolve or verify_shape in classification_metadata — since hasClass2Predicate short-circuits the provenance path entirely and hands the verdict to the async measurer, which is the highest-value fix because it removes the human from the common case; (2) revert an inert landing, since landedCommitVerdict refuses to count a reverted commit. The uiQuestion finding remains valid as the FALLBACK defect: when a gap genuinely cannot be measured the design escalates to a human via uiQuestion_write, which resolves to three vessels and logged 1000 accepted writes in 24h, while the READ shape uiQuestion has no producer at all (positive control: sibling uiFeedback resolves to two vessels). So an unmeasurable gap is also unaskable.
